creo-animal.name: Mend the Beast
creo-animal.gloss: Close a working animal's injury before the season is lost along with it. Unglamorous, and the reason the ox that hauls stone for a library is usually the same ox for thirty years.

creo-animal.name: Quicken the Herd
creo-animal.gloss: Bring a herd into season early and see it take. The primitive it moves is the same one that counts student intakes, which the faculty of medicine finds vulgar and the bursar does not.

creo-animal.name: Call the Pack
creo-animal.gloss: Make beasts, whole and willing, out of the material of the place. They are honest animals and behave like it, which is the standing complaint of everyone who has tried to use them as soldiers.

creo-animal.name: The Fat Year
creo-animal.gloss: Hold a whole countryside in abundance for a year. Towns that eat well raise more children, and the university finds out twenty years later, in the size of one entering class.

creo-animal.name: The Made Beast
creo-animal.gloss: Conjure a creature that never existed, and discover that it breeds true. The practical literature is four pages; the literature on whether one may is a shelf.

creo-aquam.name: Draw the Sweet Water
creo-aquam.gloss: Make clean water where the ground offers none. A siege is arithmetic about wells, and this working changes the arithmetic.

creo-aquam.name: The Unfailing Well
creo-aquam.gloss: A well that does not go down in a dry year. Cheap to hold, and impossible to explain to a neighbouring town whose well does.

creo-aquam.name: Turn the Channel
creo-aquam.gloss: Put a river where the mills and the fields want it. Everything downstream of the old course becomes a matter for the courts, and the courts have been busy since the working was first published.

creo-aquam.name: Raise the River
creo-aquam.gloss: Raise water out of nothing at the volume of a river, and keep raising it. The same working supplies a city and drowns a besieging camp; the treatises differ only on which use to describe first.

creo-auram.name: Turn the Wind
creo-auram.gloss: Put the wind where a mill or a drying floor wants it. The most-cast working in any university that owns farmland, and the least written about.

creo-auram.name: Clear the Sky
creo-auram.gloss: Hold weather off a place for a day. Harvest and roof-work want the same day, and a university that can promise one is immediately asked for the other.

creo-auram.name: Call the Storm
creo-auram.gloss: Evocation as the older texts meant it: weather made, aimed, and left running over a field somebody else is standing in. It is not a stronger working than the one that saves a harvest. It is that working, pointed.

creo-auram.name: The Borrowed Season
creo-auram.gloss: Keep a growing season open past the month it should have closed. Universities that hold it eat in years their neighbours do not, which has done more for enrolment than any prospectus.

creo-auram.name: Keep the Sky
creo-auram.gloss: Hold a climate over one valley indefinitely. The neighbouring valleys receive whatever is left over, and there is a long body of law about that.

creo-corpus.name: Close the Wound
creo-corpus.gloss: Knit a body back to the shape it held an hour ago. Over a career an infirmary staffed by one such mage is worth about two years to everyone who passes through it, which is the first number anyone in the discipline learns to quote.

creo-corpus.name: The Mended Decade
creo-corpus.gloss: Correct the slow failures rather than the fast ones. A physician-mage on the faculty adds most of a decade to everyone else on it, and does it quietly enough that the endowment is always the last to notice.

creo-corpus.name: Quicken the Cohort
creo-corpus.gloss: Carry a difficult birth through, at the scale of a whole population rather than a bedside. The slowest lever a god holds and the only one that compounds: a larger entering class is a larger faculty in forty years.

creo-corpus.name: The Long Tenure
creo-corpus.gloss: Twenty more years of working life for everyone who holds it. It sits at tier 3 deliberately, so that orcs — depth ceiling 3, and the shortest-lived of the six — can reach the one working that answers what is actually wrong with them.

creo-corpus.name: The Unfinished Death
creo-corpus.gloss: Hold one scholar at the point where the body has finished and the work has not. The cap is half a species' natural span, so this exhausts it for a human and is a rounding error for a dragon. The objection is not that it fails; it is that the chair has not been vacated in ninety years.

creo-fatum.name: Make the Small Luck
creo-fatum.gloss: Fortune, made in quantities too small to prove. The literature on whether it works at all is the largest in the discipline and the least conclusive.

creo-fatum.name: The Promised Year
creo-fatum.gloss: Make a promise about a year and let the year arrange itself around it. A god whose scholars can do this is asked for fewer miracles and given more.

creo-fatum.name: The Fated Hand
creo-fatum.gloss: A mage who cannot be struck is not shielded. The arrow turns out to have been aimed somewhere else the whole time, and the archer will say so under oath.

creo-fatum.name: Write the Ending
creo-fatum.gloss: Fix how a thing ends and let the middle find its own way there. Nothing survives between the third tier of this cell and this one: either the intervening work was never done, or it was done and is in no catalogue.

creo-fatum.name: The Given Destiny
creo-fatum.gloss: Give a person a fate they did not have. Every surviving instruction opens with the same warning: the caster becomes part of the fate and cannot be written out of it afterwards. Only the two deepest species can hold it at all.

creo-herbam.name: Quicken the Seed
creo-herbam.gloss: Bring a crop up in the time it takes to walk the field. The yield is unchanged; what changes is how many times in a year the field is a field.

creo-herbam.name: Grow the Beam
creo-herbam.gloss: Grow a beam already in the shape the roof wants it, joint and curve together. Carpenters who learn what it does to their trade tend to learn the working.

creo-herbam.name: Paper Without Rags
creo-herbam.gloss: Grow paper rather than beat it out of rags. A university that grows its own paper writes several times more of it, and nobody has proposed a mechanism for that other than cost.

creo-herbam.name: The Grown Hall
creo-herbam.gloss: Grow a building instead of raising one. It takes a decade and cannot be hurried past its own season, which is why the cloisters of the older universities are all exactly the same age.

creo-ignem.name: Strike the Light
creo-ignem.gloss: A flame that needs no fuel and does not go out when the window is open. The first working most universities teach, because a lamp that costs nothing buys more reading hours than any endowment.

creo-ignem.name: Hold the Temperature
creo-ignem.gloss: Keep a kiln, a forge, or a crucible at exactly one heat for as long as the work takes. Fire's entire practical literature is about holding a number still, and none of it is about throwing anything.

creo-ignem.name: The Assayer's Flame
creo-ignem.gloss: A flame pure enough that what it burns can be read off its colour. Half the metallurgy in the archive is downstream of one lamp and a patient afternoon.

creo-ignem.name: The Uncontained Hour
creo-ignem.gloss: The kiln working with the restraint taken out. It is not a separate discovery, and the literature is embarrassed about that; it is also why a fire licence is countersigned by the treasurer rather than the dean.

creo-ignem.name: The Standing Furnace
creo-ignem.gloss: A fire that feeds itself and stays where it was put. It runs the great foundries, and it denies a field to anyone who would rather not walk through a foundry.

creo-imaginem.name: Cast the Likeness
creo-imaginem.gloss: Make an image that holds still and can be walked around. The illustrated lecture, arriving centuries before cheap paper; students who have seen a thing argue about it less.

creo-imaginem.name: The Shown Interior
creo-imaginem.gloss: Show the inside of a thing without opening the thing. Anatomy, siege engines, and the workings of a lock are all taught this way, and the last of those has been raised in council more than once.

creo-imaginem.name: The Absent Scholar
creo-imaginem.gloss: Leave your likeness at the desk and be elsewhere. The standard alibi, and the standard reason a disciplinary board stopped accepting one.

creo-imaginem.name: The Crowded Hall
creo-imaginem.gloss: Fill a courtyard with people who are not there. Illusion's one honest combat use: the arrows spent on them are real, and eight is the most that will ever stand, because the ninth is always the one that gets noticed.

creo-imaginem.name: The Perfect Forgery
creo-imaginem.gloss: An image of a grimoire, accurate down to the name on every page. It reads correctly and teaches correctly, and it stops doing either on the day the mage who cast it dies — which no catalogue records.

creo-limen.name: Set the Doorstep
creo-limen.gloss: Make a threshold where the architecture provided none. A line across a floor that behaves, from then on, like a wall's business.

creo-limen.name: Draw the Circle
creo-limen.gloss: The scholar's circle, made rather than drawn: a boundary that holds because it is one, and not because chalk is persuasive.

creo-limen.name: The Made Door
creo-limen.gloss: Put a door in a wall that had none, and a corridor behind it the building did not have room for. Declares no portal effect and never will: making a threshold is not opening one, and the raid gate stays in Rego Limen (contracts.md §8).

creo-limen.name: The Threshold That Was Always There
creo-limen.gloss: Make a seam, then make it old, so that the record agrees it was always a seam. Intellego Limen reads it as genuine, which is the entire point and the reason several universities decline to teach it.

creo-mentem.name: Kindle the Question
creo-mentem.gloss: Put a question into a mind that was not asking one. Tutors call it cheating, and use it in the first week of every term.

creo-mentem.name: The Given Memory
creo-mentem.gloss: Make a memory of a lesson that was never sat through. It is indistinguishable from having learned the thing, which is the entire content of the objection to it.

creo-mentem.name: The Second Attention
creo-mentem.gloss: Make a scholar a second attention to think with, running alongside the first. It costs nothing she notices until she is sixty, and then it costs all of it at once.

creo-mentem.name: The Made Scholar
creo-mentem.gloss: A mind with no body, kept in a room, that reads. The oldest of them are older than the universities built around them, and none of them will say so.

creo-nomen.name: Give the Use-Name
creo-nomen.gloss: Attach a name to a thing that had none, and have it stick. A catalogue is impossible before this working and merely tedious after it.

creo-nomen.name: Name the Unnamed
creo-nomen.gloss: Make a true name for something that has never had one — a new working, a made beast, a hall that was grown rather than built. The name is correct, which is not the same as it being deserved.

creo-nomen.name: The Name That Teaches
creo-nomen.gloss: Build a name so that holding it conveys the thing named. In a True Naming universe this is a term's curriculum in one syllable, and it is why those universities' terms are shorter.

creo-nomen.name: The Second Name
creo-nomen.gloss: Make yourself a second true name, so that the first can be spent. Perdo Nomen can take a name away; this puts a spare on the shelf, and a mage holding both is difficult to end and impossible to cite.

creo-terram.name: Make the Brick
creo-terram.gloss: Stone out of nothing, one brick at a time, at a price in mage-months no quarry would survive being compared to. The point is not the brick; it is that the brick appears where no cart can go.

creo-terram.name: The Poured Wall
creo-terram.gloss: Make a wall as a single piece, with no courses for anything to fail along. Perdo Terram takes considerably longer with these, which is the argument that gets them funded.

creo-terram.name: The Conjured Vein
creo-terram.gloss: Make ore in the ground, in the shape ore takes, where a survey would expect to find it. Three universities' worth of argument exists on whether conjured silver is silver; the mints hold their own view.

creo-terram.name: The Raised Bastion
creo-terram.gloss: Raise a fortification in an afternoon, out of material that was not there in the morning. Every siege doctrine written before the working assumes a wall takes a season, and all of them are still on the syllabus.

creo-umbra.name: Cast the Shadow
creo-umbra.gloss: Make a shadow where nothing stands to cast one. Trivial, and the first half of everything else in the form.

creo-umbra.name: The Lengthened Dusk
creo-umbra.gloss: Hold the hour after sunset over a place for as long as attention lasts. Guards keep the watch they were rostered for and not the one the light says they should.

creo-umbra.name: The Kept Shadow
creo-umbra.gloss: Put a thing into a shadow and take it out again later. A library kept this way cannot be burned and can be lost by forgetting which wall it was cast on; the Art of Memory faculty consider the whole approach plagiarism.

creo-umbra.name: The Unlit Hall
creo-umbra.gloss: Take a building out of the light entirely. Raiding parties have crossed the courtyard, emptied the wrong hall, and left with the library standing behind them.

creo-vim.name: Kindle the Aura
creo-vim.gloss: Thicken the magic of a place the way one banks a fire. Everything cast in the room afterwards is easier, and nobody can say by how much without casting it twice.

creo-vim.name: Feed the Working
creo-vim.gloss: Pour raw magic into a working that is already running, including somebody else's. The etiquette around doing this uninvited is older than most of the universities that teach it.

creo-vim.name: The Standing Aura
creo-vim.gloss: Make a place permanently easier to work in. This is why universities sit where they sit, and why the ones that were sited for the river have all quietly moved.

creo-vim.name: The Warded Precinct
creo-vim.gloss: Make enough raw magic in one place that it stands between what is cast at the precinct and the precinct. Nothing about it is clever: it is a wall built out of the same stuff as the arrow.

creo-vim.name: The Made Vis
creo-vim.gloss: Magic made rather than gathered. Every economy in the multiverse is priced on the assumption that this is impossible, and the four universities that hold it have each independently decided not to publish.

intellego-animal.name: Cut the Sign
intellego-animal.gloss: Take an hour-old print for everything it is: what made it, what weight it was carrying, and whether it was hurrying away from something that is still nearby.

intellego-animal.name: Number the Herd
intellego-animal.gloss: Know how many, of what ages, and which of them will not see the winter — without penning a single animal to be looked at. Herders who have it stop losing the whole beast to find out it was sick.

intellego-animal.name: Chart the Migration
intellego-animal.gloss: Know where the herds will be a season before the herds have decided. The first working in this cell that pays for a granary rather than a supper.

intellego-animal.name: The Beast's Own Eye
intellego-animal.gloss: Borrow what an animal is looking at, from wherever it happens to be standing. A scholar whose watchmen are all crows is difficult to surprise, and impossible to catch listening — nothing she posted can be questioned afterwards.

intellego-aquam.name: Sound the Well
intellego-aquam.gloss: Find how deep the water truly sits, and whether it will still be sitting there in August, without lowering a rope into it.

intellego-aquam.name: Sip the Standing Pool
intellego-aquam.gloss: Learn what is in a water before drinking enough of it to learn the ordinary way. Whole siege years turn on which of a city's three cisterns is the one that kills.

intellego-aquam.name: Trace the Current
intellego-aquam.gloss: Follow a moving water back to where it comes from and forward to where it means to go, including the stretches of it that are underground and the stretches that are somebody else's.

intellego-aquam.name: Fathom the Watershed
intellego-aquam.gloss: Hold every water of a country in one perception at once — springs, seeps, the river's bad years, the marsh that used to be a lake. Mills get sited on this, and so do the arguments about who owns the rain.

intellego-auram.name: The Ache Before Rain
intellego-auram.gloss: The old soldier's knee, made deliberate and made accurate. Three days' warning saves more harvests than any working of Creo, and costs a university nothing to keep.

intellego-auram.name: Gauge the Wind's Road
intellego-auram.gloss: Perceive the wind aloft, which is not the wind you are standing in and rarely agrees with it. Everything that sails or grinds is scheduled against this.

intellego-auram.name: Reckon the Season
intellego-auram.gloss: Take a whole year's weather in advance, coarsely, and be right about it more often than not. Coarse and usually right is worth more to a granary than precise and occasional.

intellego-auram.name: The Lightning's Chosen Ground
intellego-auram.gloss: Know which stone the storm has already picked, and put the library on a different one. Universities that hold this working lose towers at a rate their neighbours find suspicious.

intellego-corpus.name: Take the Pulse
intellego-corpus.gloss: Two fingers at a wrist, and the whole of what the body is currently doing about itself. Every physician thinks she can already do this; the ones who can are the ones who stop being surprised.

intellego-corpus.name: Sift the Humours
intellego-corpus.gloss: Separate what is wrong with a body from what is merely unusual about it. The great saving is not in the cures it enables but in the ones it stops a physician from attempting.

intellego-corpus.name: Listen at the Ribs
intellego-corpus.gloss: Attend to the sounds a body makes only on the inside, and know which of them is new. Everything worth catching is quiet for a year first.

intellego-corpus.name: Tell the Hour of a Body
intellego-corpus.gloss: Say how long this body has, from the body alone. It is not fate — Fatum reads the hour that was appointed; this reads only the hour the flesh is already walking toward, which is why it can be argued with.

intellego-fatum.name: Cast the Lots
intellego-fatum.gloss: The oldest divination there is, made honest. The lots were always random; this working is the part that makes them not, and every student's first result is indistinguishable from luck.

intellego-fatum.name: The Omen and the Coincidence
intellego-fatum.gloss: Separate the sign that means something from the enormous number of things that merely happened. This is the entire discipline, and the reason Fatum scholars are so tiresome about method.

intellego-fatum.name: The Fork Seen From Above
intellego-fatum.gloss: Stand outside a decision and see both roads to their ends at once. Applied to research it says which line of enquiry pays; applied to a student it says which one is worth the hours, which is the part the faculty argues about.

intellego-fatum.name: The Appointed Hour
intellego-fatum.gloss: Know the hour the world has set aside for you. It does not move. But a scholar who knows which afternoon to spend indoors buys back all the years that were never appointed at all, and most deaths were never appointed.

intellego-fatum.name: The Thread Fate Set Down
intellego-fatum.gloss: Perceive your own thread so exactly that you can tell the moment fate puts it down to attend to someone else — and live in those moments. Nothing that works by destiny can find a mage who is not currently being tracked by it. Archmages who hold it tend to have no recorded death.

intellego-herbam.name: Sight the Blight
intellego-herbam.gloss: See the rot in a field on the morning it decides to happen, rather than on the morning it shows.

intellego-herbam.name: Question the Orchard
intellego-herbam.gloss: Put the question to the trees themselves — what they are short of, what they are hoarding, which of them is dying quietly and taking the row with it.

intellego-herbam.name: Pick Out the Simple
intellego-herbam.gloss: Know a medicinal herb by its leaf, its hour, and its ground, and know it apart from the four things in the same hedge that will kill the patient instead. Most of herb-lore is the apart-from.

intellego-herbam.name: The Root Beneath the Root
intellego-herbam.gloss: Perceive the thing a forest is doing under the soil, where it is not a thousand trees but one argument. Foresters who learn it stop calling the wood a crop, which their treasurers dislike.

intellego-ignem.name: Judge the Kiln
intellego-ignem.gloss: Know the state of a fire without opening the door to it, which is the only way to know the state of a fire.

intellego-ignem.name: The Colour of Ready Iron
intellego-ignem.gloss: Smiths have always read heat by colour and always argued about it. This settles the argument, and a smithy that stops arguing produces roughly a third more.

intellego-ignem.name: Scry the Coals
intellego-ignem.gloss: The old fire-gazing, done properly. What returns is not a picture but a pressure, and the discipline is entirely in refusing to improve it into a picture on the way to the page.

intellego-ignem.name: Where the Fire Will Go
intellego-ignem.gloss: Perceive a fire's whole future path through a building before it has taken the first yard of it. Fire-wardens use it to choose what to wet; the other profession that wants it uses it to choose what not to.

intellego-imaginem.name: Catch the Painted Thing
intellego-imaginem.gloss: Notice that what you are looking at is a picture of itself. The first lesson is that the tell is never in the image; it is in how little the image is bothering to be looked at from the side.

intellego-imaginem.name: Watch the Light Lie
intellego-imaginem.gloss: Attend to the mechanism of a false image rather than to the image. Knowing exactly how a thing is not seen is the first half of not being seen, and this cell reaches concealment from that side rather than from hiding.

intellego-imaginem.name: The Room You Are Not In
intellego-imaginem.gloss: Take the sight and sound of a place you are nowhere near, entire, without sending anything there to fetch it. Every treaty on scrying is really about this working, and none of them has ever been enforceable.

intellego-imaginem.name: Nothing Painted Passes
intellego-imaginem.gloss: No false image within reach survives being looked at. The same perception run backwards tells the mage precisely where the looking in a room is going, and she is never standing there.

intellego-limen.name: Sense the Seam
intellego-limen.gloss: Feel the exact line at which one place stops being itself. A student who has it stops walking into doorways she did not know were there.

intellego-limen.name: Count the Doors
intellego-limen.gloss: Enumerate every threshold in a place at once — its gates, its grave-lines, the seams nobody built on purpose.

intellego-limen.name: Read the Binding
intellego-limen.gloss: Read a closed threshold for what it was closed against, and by whom, and how long ago they stopped renewing it.

intellego-limen.name: Stand in the Doorway
intellego-limen.gloss: Hold the seam itself. A mage who is neither inside nor out is difficult to look at directly, and harder still to remember having seen.

intellego-mentem.name: Weigh the Attention
intellego-mentem.gloss: Tell whether you are being listened to, and by how much of a mind.

intellego-mentem.name: Follow the Thought
intellego-mentem.gloss: Watch a thought move through a mind that is not yours. The best professors have always seemed to know exactly where a student got lost; this is how.

intellego-mentem.name: Read the Surface
intellego-mentem.gloss: Take what is already at the front of a mind. Nothing is broken and nothing is missed, which is what makes it so hard to prosecute.

intellego-mentem.name: Open the Locked Room
intellego-mentem.gloss: Go past what a scholar is thinking to what she has decided not to think about. The first of the two theft vectors, and the one that leaves the victim intact.

intellego-nomen.name: Hear the Name Spoken
intellego-nomen.gloss: Notice that a thing has a name at all, which most people go their whole lives without doing.

intellego-nomen.name: Spell the Lesser Name
intellego-nomen.gloss: Set down a use-name accurately enough that a scribe who never met the thing can copy it without spoiling it.

intellego-nomen.name: Derive the True Name
intellego-nomen.gloss: Work a true name out from first principles rather than being told it. Slow, and the only method that does not put you in someone's debt.

intellego-nomen.name: The Catalogue of Names
intellego-nomen.gloss: Order names against one another so that a new one can be found by where the gap in the shelf is. Libraries built on it outlive the mages who filled them.

intellego-terram.name: Taste the Soil
intellego-terram.gloss: Know what the ground under a field will give up before a season is wasted on it.

intellego-terram.name: Survey the Strata
intellego-terram.gloss: Read a hillside as the stack of pages it is, and say which page the good stone is on.

intellego-terram.name: Find the Deep Seam
intellego-terram.gloss: Follow a vein down past where digging by guess stops paying. Whole universities have been sited on one casting of this.

intellego-terram.name: Read the Fault
intellego-terram.gloss: See where the ground intends to fail. Knowing where a wall cannot stand is the cheapest possible way to learn where it can — and it sits at tier 3 deliberately, so that orcs, whose depth ceiling is 3, can reach a build-rate working at all.

intellego-umbra.name: The Second Shadow
intellego-umbra.gloss: Notice that something in the room is casting one shadow more than it is entitled to. Half the students who learn it stop sleeping well; the other half stop being surprised by anything.

intellego-umbra.name: What the Shadow Remembers
intellego-umbra.gloss: A shadow is a record of an absence, and records can be interrogated. Ask an empty patch of floor what stood in it, and it will tell you the shape, though never the name.

intellego-umbra.name: Look Along the Shadow
intellego-umbra.gloss: Sight down a shadow toward the thing that is casting it, and keep going. What is on the far side of the wall is not hidden from the shadow, only from you, and the shadow can be asked.

intellego-umbra.name: The Unlit Line
intellego-umbra.gloss: Perceive, continuously and without effort, which line through a room no eye is currently on — and be on it. Nothing about the mage is hidden. She is simply never where the looking is happening.

intellego-umbra.name: The Shadow Before the Thing
intellego-umbra.gloss: Some shadows arrive first. A raid throws one across a floor three days ahead of itself, and a mage who has learned to read the early ones is standing somewhere else by the time the caster gets there. This is where shadow stops being optics and starts being fate.

intellego-vim.name: Feel the Air Go Tight
intellego-vim.gloss: The small pull in a room in the moment before something is cast in it. Students describe it as a held breath that is not theirs, and the ones who never feel it are usually the ones who die indoors.

intellego-vim.name: Price the Working
intellego-vim.gloss: Say what a spell cost the mage who cast it. Half of scholarship is knowing which rival results were expensive, because those are the ones nobody bothered to fake.

intellego-vim.name: The Residue in the Room
intellego-vim.gloss: Perceive what was cast in a place after the casting is over — a day after, in a still room, three weeks. Most of what a university knows about its neighbours was picked up off a floor.

intellego-vim.name: Know the Hand That Cast It
intellego-vim.gloss: Every mage casts with an accent. This reads it, and names the school, the teacher, and often the individual. Raids are attributed by it, and at least two wars in the archive were begun on a careful misreading of one.

muto-animal.name: Turn the Coat
muto-animal.gloss: Move a beast's coat into a season it is not in. The wool comes off thick in high summer and the animal spends the rest of the year disagreeing with the weather.

muto-animal.name: The Willing Ox
muto-animal.gloss: Change what a beast is shaped to pull. The change is worn, not granted: the shoulders go back to being an ox's shoulders in a season, and the carter is expected to know when.

muto-animal.name: The Changed Kennel
muto-animal.gloss: Turn a kennel into something no one will call a kennel by morning. The dogs are still the dogs, which is the part that unsettles the people who have to feed them afterwards.

muto-animal.name: What the Beast Remembers
muto-animal.gloss: Hold a herd in its changed shape long enough to march it somewhere. Every animal so held is counting down to its own shape, and a field commander's whole skill is in knowing the count.

muto-aquam.name: Sweeten the Cistern
muto-aquam.gloss: Turn foul water into water. Not clean water — water, which is a lower standard than the phrase suggests and has founded more towns than any other working in the cell.

muto-aquam.name: Thicken the Ford
muto-aquam.gloss: Change a river into something that will bear a loaded cart. It bears the cart and not the carter, or the carter and not the cart, depending on which the caster was thinking about.

muto-aquam.name: The Standing River
muto-aquam.gloss: Turn a current into a thing that has stopped agreeing to be crossed. It is not a wall and it is not frozen; it is a river with its mind changed, and it changes back.

muto-aquam.name: The River Remembers Salt
muto-aquam.gloss: Any water that was ever sea can be persuaded that it still is. Persuading it is cheap; persuading it back is a matter for the next generation of whoever farms the valley.

muto-auram.name: Turn the Wind
muto-auram.gloss: Change which way the air has decided to go. Mills, sails, and drying-floors all run on the assumption that this is legal here, and half of them stop when it is not.

muto-auram.name: The Mild Season
muto-auram.gloss: Turn a bad year into an ordinary one. The weather it was going to be is not destroyed, only converted, and the standing question in the literature is where the conversion is paid for.

muto-auram.name: The Air That Carries Nothing
muto-auram.gloss: Change air into air that will not pass a sound or a scent along. Everything inside it is still there and still shouting; the air has simply stopped consenting to relay it.

muto-auram.name: The Storm Turned Inward
muto-auram.gloss: Change a storm's argument with the horizon into an argument with the ground beneath it. Weather so turned keeps its old heading and comes back around on the caster within the week.

muto-corpus.name: Borrowed Hands
muto-corpus.gloss: Take the hands of a trade you never trained in. Copyists hired for their fingers rather than their letters are a known and faintly disreputable feature of large libraries.

muto-corpus.name: The Body for the Work
muto-corpus.gloss: Change a body to suit its labour rather than changing the labour to suit the body. Masons who hold it finish walls early and are unfit for anything else by fifty.

muto-corpus.name: Wear Another Face
muto-corpus.gloss: Change the flesh, not the appearance of it. An illusionist's version washes off in a hard rain; this one has to be worn back, and the walk is what gives you away either way.

muto-corpus.name: The Long Body
muto-corpus.gloss: Rearrange a body so that it wears at a different rate. It is not the same thing as being young, and every scholar who has held it says so in exactly the same tired sentence.

muto-corpus.name: The Shape That Holds
muto-corpus.gloss: A change that no longer has to be renewed, only endured. Transformation is never finished, so what this actually buys is a body that has stopped trying to finish going back.

muto-fatum.name: Turn the Small Luck
muto-fatum.gloss: Change a trivial fate into a different trivial fate. The dropped cup lands whole and the milk is sour instead. Nothing is gained; something is exchanged, which is the entire cell in one sentence and the reason it is taught first.

muto-fatum.name: Change the Debt
muto-fatum.gloss: Move a fate off the person it was addressed to and onto a thing that person owns. The ruin still happens. It happens to the barn.

muto-fatum.name: The Later Appointment
muto-fatum.gloss: Change the hour at which a fate falls due, and nothing else about it whatsoever. The appointment is kept; it has merely been rescheduled, and the literature is unanimous that it will not be rescheduled twice.

muto-fatum.name: Divide It Among the Heirs
muto-fatum.gloss: Change a fate that belongs to a person into one that belongs to a line, so that it is paid in instalments by people who did not incur it. Houses that hold this working are large, prosperous, and quiet about why.

muto-fatum.name: The Fate That Was Yours
muto-fatum.gloss: Exchange one whole fate for another whole fate, entire, with something that has one. Both parties survive the working and neither is afterwards the person the archive holds on file. The archive is not wrong.

muto-herbam.name: Season the Green Wood
muto-herbam.gloss: Turn green timber into seasoned timber without spending the years on it. The beam is honest about having been hurried, and a good carpenter can hear it in the tap of a mallet.

muto-herbam.name: The Second Harvest
muto-herbam.gloss: Change a crop into a crop the year actually needs, after the year has made itself clear. Nothing is created; a field of straw becomes a smaller field of grain.

muto-herbam.name: The Grown Beam
muto-herbam.gloss: Change a living tree into the shape a joint wants, and leave it living while it takes. Halls built this way cannot be repaired by anyone who does not also hold the working.

muto-herbam.name: The Thicket That Was a Road
muto-herbam.gloss: Turn a road into the wood it was cut from. It remembers being a road and is one again inside three seasons, which is the whole trouble with using it in a siege you intend to win slowly.

muto-ignem.name: Bank the Forge
muto-ignem.gloss: Turn a fire's heat into a slower and longer heat of the same total. Smelting that would take a week takes a week, and takes one charge of fuel to do it.

muto-ignem.name: The Cold Flame
muto-ignem.gloss: Turn a fire's heat into its opposite while it goes on burning. It still consumes; it has only been changed about what. Standing in it is survivable and is not pleasant.

muto-ignem.name: Teach the Fire What to Eat
muto-ignem.gloss: Change what a fire counts as fuel. Stone will do, once it has been told; the fire is slower about stone and does not otherwise object.

muto-ignem.name: The Heat That Was a Hearth
muto-ignem.gloss: Every fire in a building was lit by somebody for a reason. This changes the reason, and leaves the fire exactly where its owner put it.

muto-imaginem.name: Turn the Diagram
muto-imaginem.gloss: Change a mechanism's appearance into the appearance of its own structure. Students stop asking what is inside it, because what is inside it is now what they are looking at.

muto-imaginem.name: The Lecture Made Visible
muto-imaginem.gloss: Turn an argument into something the room can watch happening. It is the same argument and it is not improved; it has only stopped needing to be held in the head to be followed.

muto-imaginem.name: Wear the Room
muto-imaginem.gloss: Change your image into the image of whatever is behind you. It fails on anyone who has been looking at you continuously, which is a shorter list than it sounds.

muto-imaginem.name: The Image That Argues Back
muto-imaginem.gloss: Turn a demonstration into one that changes in response to the student's error. The lecturer is still doing the work; she has merely stopped being in the room while it is done.

muto-limen.name: Change What the Wall Means
muto-limen.gloss: A wall raised against weather can be persuaded it was raised against people. It was not, and it knows, so the persuasion has to be renewed about as often as a sentry is changed.

muto-limen.name: The Door That Was a Window
muto-limen.gloss: Change a threshold's kind rather than its state. Declares no portal effect and never will: opening onto another sky is Rego Limen, and contracts.md §8 keeps it there on purpose.

muto-limen.name: Which Side the Courtyard Is On
muto-limen.gloss: Change which side of a boundary a place is on without moving the boundary or the place. Two sieges in the record were settled by an argument about a courtyard, conducted entirely in this working.

muto-limen.name: The Seam Made a Hinge
muto-limen.gloss: Change a boundary into a joint, so that it bends where it used to hold. It bends back, and the fortress it was worked on is afterwards a fortress with a habit.

muto-mentem.name: Turn the Difficulty
muto-mentem.gloss: Change a problem's shape in a mind until it is a problem that mind already knows how to have. Nothing has been solved. The solving now costs what an easy problem costs.

muto-mentem.name: The Changed Appetite
muto-mentem.gloss: Change what a mind wants to think about, rather than what it is permitted to. Compulsion is Rego and shows; this does not show, including to the scholar it was worked on.

muto-mentem.name: Translate the Expert
muto-mentem.gloss: Change another scholar's knowledge into the shape your own mind keeps things in. She keeps hers. What you carry off is a translation, and translations lose things. Universities that count two theft vectors are counting the two that are prosecutable.

muto-mentem.name: The Mind Made a Library
muto-mentem.gloss: Change a mind's arrangement into a catalogue's. It is reversible in the way everything in Muto is reversible, and the scholars who reverse it go on thinking in shelves regardless.

muto-nomen.name: Alter One Letter
muto-nomen.gloss: Change a true name by the smallest amount that is still a change. The thing changes by the same amount. Most of what is known about naming was learned by doing this to unimportant objects and writing down how they were afterwards slightly different unimportant objects.

muto-nomen.name: Lend the Name
muto-nomen.gloss: Give a thing your name to hold for an afternoon. Nothing that hunts by naming can tell you from a chair, and nothing that hunts by naming can tell the chair from you, which is the half that has to be planned for.

muto-nomen.name: Call It Iron Until It Is
muto-nomen.gloss: Change the true name of poor rock to the true name of iron and then wait. It becomes iron at roughly the rate the claim goes unchallenged, and stops the moment anyone successfully contradicts it. Assayers are paid well and are not popular.

muto-nomen.name: Trade True Names
muto-nomen.gloss: Exchange true names with another mage, so that each becomes the other in every way naming can reach. Compulsion follows the name. Skill does not. Both parties spend the arrangement being ordered about in a discipline they cannot practise.

muto-nomen.name: The Second True Name
muto-nomen.gloss: Hold a second true name without surrendering the first. Nothing in the discipline says a thing may have two. Nothing in the discipline says it may not. The holder is betting a great deal on which of those two silences is the load-bearing one.

muto-terram.name: Soften the Stone
muto-terram.gloss: Turn cut stone briefly workable. The masons have the length of an afternoon and no more, and every quarry in the subset has a bell for it.

muto-terram.name: Turn the Poor Ore
muto-terram.gloss: Change worthless rock into ore that is merely bad. Never into good ore: the working improves a thing by one step and has never once been made to take two.

muto-terram.name: The Stone That Was Sand
muto-terram.gloss: Turn a riverbank into ashlar. It knows it was sand and intends to be sand again, so a wall raised from it is a wall you have agreed to build twice.

muto-terram.name: Turn the Ground Under Them
muto-terram.gloss: Change standing ground into the sand it was before anyone stood on it. The besiegers of Halvard's Rock reported that the ground did not open; it simply stopped having been a floor.

muto-umbra.name: Turn the Shadow
muto-umbra.gloss: Change the direction a shadow falls without moving what casts it. Nobody notices, in the sense that nobody can afterwards say what it was they noticed.

muto-umbra.name: The Shadow of Something Else
muto-umbra.gloss: Change what your shadow is a shadow of. The old shape is still in it and comes back at the hour the working was first laid, which is why this is taught alongside a clock.

muto-umbra.name: Give the Shade Weight
muto-umbra.gloss: Turn shade into something with an opinion about being walked through. It is cold in the way deep water is cold, and it is exactly as deep as whatever cast it is tall.

muto-umbra.name: Trade Shadows
muto-umbra.gloss: Exchange your shadow for another's and step where theirs may go. The other party keeps yours for the duration, and anything that hunts by shadow can still find you with it.

muto-vim.name: Turn the Working
muto-vim.gloss: Change a small spell into a different small spell while it is still being cast. The first thing every apprentice does with it is ruin a working she had already finished paying for.

muto-vim.name: Convert the Form
muto-vim.gloss: Change what a working is about without changing what it does — Ignem to Aquam and back again. The grid is not a filing system for scholars; this is the working that proves it.

muto-vim.name: Turn the Incoming
muto-vim.gloss: Change a hostile working, in flight, into a harmless one of the same size. It arrives on time and does something else, and the caster is not told which.

muto-vim.name: The Second Tradition
muto-vim.gloss: Change how a working is performed rather than what it performs: a memorised formula rewritten as a room in a palace. The translation costs about a third of the working, in both directions, every time.

muto-vim.name: The Common Root
muto-vim.gloss: Change any working into any other by way of what the two were before they were told apart. Every scholar who has published on it has published the same warning, in the same words: the way back is not the way you came.

perdo-animal.name: Founder the Horse
perdo-animal.gloss: Unmake the wind in a beast at a gallop. The rider is not thrown and is not hurt; she is simply on foot, in a field, a long way from her line.

perdo-animal.name: Nothing Takes the Scent
perdo-animal.gloss: Unmake what you left in the air behind you. The hounds are not confused — a confused hound casts about. These sit down.

perdo-animal.name: Empty the Pasture
perdo-animal.gloss: Wither a holding's beasts across a stretch of ground, over an afternoon, without a mark on any of them. A siege begun in spring is decided by this in autumn.

perdo-animal.name: Nothing Answers the Horn
perdo-animal.gloss: Unmake what was called. Warhorses, hounds, the summoned things a Nomen mage keeps on a name — all of it goes, and the field is very quiet, and the horn is blown twice more before anyone stops.

perdo-aquam.name: Thirst
perdo-aquam.gloss: Unmake the water a body is carrying, beginning with the water it can spare. There is a good deal of it, and then there is not.

perdo-aquam.name: Unwrite
perdo-aquam.gloss: Take the water out of ink. The page is not burned, the binding is not cut, and the book is a stack of blank leaves taking up exactly as much shelf as it did. Raiders who cannot carry a library and will not burn one use this.

perdo-aquam.name: The Dry Season
perdo-aquam.gloss: Unmake the water in the ground itself, across a stretch of it. The wells go first, then the shallow roots, then the arguments about whose fault it is.

perdo-aquam.name: Leave Them the Salt
perdo-aquam.gloss: Unmake every fresh water in reach and leave behind only what cannot be drunk. A holding treated this way is not stormed. It is walked into, eleven days later.

perdo-auram.name: Take the Breath
perdo-auram.gloss: Unmake the air a body has already drawn. She does not gasp — there is nothing left to gasp with — and it is the surprise on the face that wardens remember afterwards.

perdo-auram.name: Unmake the Gale
perdo-auram.gloss: Take the weather out of weather that was aimed at you. The storm does not break and does not turn; it stops being a storm, midway, above the men it was meant for.

perdo-auram.name: The Airless Room
perdo-auram.gloss: Unmake the air inside a closed space and hold it unmade. It is the cheapest working on this ladder and the one universities most often decline to teach, for reasons that are about doors rather than about air.

perdo-auram.name: The Sky Withdraws
perdo-auram.gloss: Unmake the air over a field. Nothing flies, nothing carries, nothing burns, and no order shouted at the far end of the line is heard at this one. Both sides suffer it equally, which is the whole of the argument against it.

perdo-corpus.name: Wither the Hand
perdo-corpus.gloss: Take the strength out of the hand that is holding the sword. It is not a wound, and it does not mend the way a wound does.

perdo-corpus.name: The Long Fever
perdo-corpus.gloss: Unmake a body slowly enough that the physicians name the illness, argue about it, and are wrong in a way that takes them six weeks to be wrong in.

perdo-corpus.name: Take the Years
perdo-corpus.gloss: Unmake the decades a body still had in front of it. She is not injured. She is older than she was this morning, and the work she was going to do is not going to be done by her.

perdo-corpus.name: The Hand That Wrote It
perdo-corpus.gloss: The standard answer to a scholar who is the last surviving instance of something. It is not a duel and it is not a battle. It is a piece of archival policy, carried out by someone who was paid for it and told very little.

perdo-fatum.name: Spoil the Omen
perdo-fatum.gloss: Unmake a sign before anyone has read it. The augur is not wrong. There is simply nothing there for her to be right about.

perdo-fatum.name: Take the Luck
perdo-fatum.gloss: Unmake a person's share of things going well. Nothing happens to her. Things merely stop not happening to her.

perdo-fatum.name: Nothing Is Owed
perdo-fatum.gloss: Every fate is a debt something means to collect. Unmake the debt and the collector goes elsewhere; unmake enough of them and the world stops keeping accounts in your name at all.

perdo-fatum.name: Where Nothing Turns Out
perdo-fatum.gloss: Unmake, across a field, the tendency of events to come to anything. Charges arrive late. Signals are not seen. Both sides bleed and neither wins, and the mage who cast it was not trying to win either.

perdo-fatum.name: The Unmade Discovery
perdo-fatum.gloss: It does not destroy a node. It unmakes the arrival of one. Somewhere a scholar who was going to derive something puts her pen down for a reason she could give you, and it is not the reason. The universities that do not hold this working cannot prove that they do not.

perdo-herbam.name: Wither the Row
perdo-herbam.gloss: Unmake a row of a crop at the root. Done at the edge of a field it reads as bad drainage, and that is the point of doing it at the edge.

perdo-herbam.name: Take the Haft
perdo-herbam.gloss: Unmake the wood in a thing that everyone thinks of as iron. Spears become spearheads, ladders become rungs, and a siege engine becomes a great deal of rope and a heap of fittings.

perdo-herbam.name: The Failed Harvest
perdo-herbam.gloss: Wither a season across a stretch of ground. The dead are counted the following winter, attributed to the weather, and no mage is named anywhere in the accounting.

perdo-herbam.name: The Shelves Give Way
perdo-herbam.gloss: A library is stone and glass and a very great deal of wood. Unmake the presses, the shelving, and the boards the bindings are stretched over, and what is on the floor afterwards is not a collection. It is loose paper in the dark, in an order nobody wrote down.

perdo-ignem.name: Snuff
perdo-ignem.gloss: Take the fire out of a flame. The wick is not wet and no smoke rises, and the room is a room that a moment ago had a light in it.

perdo-ignem.name: Take the Warmth
perdo-ignem.gloss: Unmake the heat inside a body rather than the body. Corpus withers the flesh; this leaves the flesh entirely alone and takes away the thing that was keeping it going.

perdo-ignem.name: The Unburnt Library
perdo-ignem.gloss: Unmake a fire that is already in the stacks. Perdo is how a library is saved rather less often than it is how one is lost, and it is the same working either way — the same training, the same hour of practice, different people holding it.

perdo-ignem.name: Nothing Will Catch
perdo-ignem.gloss: Take the willingness to burn out of a place. Nothing here will catch: not the thatch, not the oil, not the shelves. Not the hearth either, and not the lamp a scholar reads by. Universities that keep this standing have not had a fire in a century and cannot say what the century cost them.

perdo-imaginem.name: Take the Likeness
perdo-imaginem.gloss: Unmake the resemblance between a thing and its picture. The portrait is still a portrait. It is simply not of anyone.

perdo-imaginem.name: The Quiet Working
perdo-imaginem.gloss: Unmake the sound and the light a casting makes, and not the casting. Wardens who watch are expensive and wardens who listen are cheap, and this is the working that decided which kind a university hires.

perdo-imaginem.name: Unmake the Demonstration
perdo-imaginem.gloss: The professor's hands still move and the working still happens; there is nothing to see it by. Aimed at demonstrations, and afterwards at the engraved plates in the treatises made from them. The working survives. The picture of it does not, and after one generation those are the same thing.

perdo-imaginem.name: No One Can Describe It
perdo-imaginem.gloss: Unmake the image of a place and leave the place. Scouts come back having seen nothing they can put in a report; two maps of it disagree with each other and with the ground. The hall is exactly where it always was, and the company sent to hold it does not arrive.

perdo-limen.name: Fray the Edge
perdo-limen.gloss: Wear at a boundary until it stops being certain about where it is. Contains no portal-stability effect, and may never gain one (contracts.md §1.6).

perdo-limen.name: Unhinge
perdo-limen.gloss: Take the held-shut out of a shut thing. Wards fail first at the place they were joined.

perdo-limen.name: The Open Wound
perdo-limen.gloss: Leave a threshold unmade rather than merely opened, so that the ground on both sides of it stays wrong for a while.

perdo-limen.name: Nothing Holds
perdo-limen.gloss: Unmake every seam in reach at once. Defenders describe it as the moment a fortress stops being one building and starts being a pile of walls.

perdo-mentem.name: Blunt the Edge
perdo-mentem.gloss: Take the sharpness out of an attention. The victim is not hurt and cannot say what is wrong, only that thinking has begun to cost more than it did.

perdo-mentem.name: The Misplaced Hour
perdo-mentem.gloss: Unmake a stretch of a mind's own record of itself. Small, deniable, and the first thing every inquiry into a scholar's death asks about.

perdo-mentem.name: Scatter the Lesson
perdo-mentem.gloss: Undo a thing at the moment it is being taught, in every mind in the room. Aimed at lecture halls, and used on them.

perdo-mentem.name: Unmake the Mind
perdo-mentem.gloss: Not kill. Unmake — the body walks out of the hall and the scholar does not. This is the working the vision's flagship interdiction forbids by name: Mentem is open to my scholars, but none shall unmake a mind.

perdo-mentem.name: The Empty Room
perdo-mentem.gloss: The unmaking held open, so that nothing put back into the space stays there either. Universities that permit it do not admit to it.

perdo-nomen.name: Mispronounce
perdo-nomen.gloss: Damage a name slightly, in the mouth of whoever is trying to use it on you.

perdo-nomen.name: Shed the Use-Name
perdo-nomen.gloss: Unmake the name you are called by. Colleagues still recognise the face; nothing that works by naming can find you at all.

perdo-nomen.name: Unsay the Name
perdo-nomen.gloss: Turn the working on someone else's true name. What is left is not injured; it is less.

perdo-nomen.name: The Nameless
perdo-nomen.gloss: Hold your own unnaming indefinitely. Cheap to maintain, ruinous to explain to an heir, and the reason some archmages have no biography.

perdo-terram.name: Crumble
perdo-terram.gloss: Take the bind out of mortar, one course at a time.

perdo-terram.name: Open the Ground
perdo-terram.gloss: Unmake the ground's willingness to be stood on, across a stretch of it, for as long as attention holds.

perdo-terram.name: Pull Down the Arch
perdo-terram.gloss: Unmake the one stone the rest were argued into leaning on. Cheaper than unmaking a building, and identical in outcome.

perdo-terram.name: The Swallowed Hall
perdo-terram.gloss: Take a building's foundation out from under it and leave the hole behaving badly afterwards. The standard answer to a library that cannot be carried away.

perdo-umbra.name: Thin the Shade
perdo-umbra.gloss: Wear at what a thing leaves behind it. The shadow is still there and no longer quite belongs to anyone, and the thing that cast it is, by a small amount, less.

perdo-umbra.name: Lay the Shade
perdo-umbra.gloss: The dead leave a shape. Unmake the shape. Wardens who do this are paid by the hour and never by the name, and are not asked afterwards what the shape had been doing.

perdo-umbra.name: Nothing Casts Here
perdo-umbra.gloss: Unmake every remnant across a stretch of ground and hold it unmade, so that nothing which happens there has an afterward. Fought over twice, such a field is not haunted, and the villages near it find that worse.

perdo-umbra.name: Make Sure
perdo-umbra.gloss: A scholar who dies holding something nobody else holds leaves a shade that still, faintly, holds it — enough for a patient Intellego man and a long night in the right graveyard. This unmakes the shade. Whoever commissions it is not being cruel. She is making sure.

perdo-vim.name: Let It Lapse
perdo-vim.gloss: Do not argue with a working. Unmake the part of it that intends to keep going, and then wait a moment.

perdo-vim.name: The Unfinished Sentence
perdo-vim.gloss: Unmake a working while it is still being made. Far cheaper than unmaking a finished one, and the reason a duel between equals is decided in the first half-second and watched for the remaining hour.

perdo-vim.name: Where Nothing Takes
perdo-vim.gloss: Unmake, over a stretch of ground, the willingness of workings to hold at all — your own among them. It declares no portal-stability effect and never will (contracts.md §1.6). The cell stops at three nodes on purpose: further down, unmaking magic stops being a spell and starts being a rule, and rules belong to the god.

rego-animal.name: The Quiet Halter
rego-animal.gloss: Compel a beast to stand where it was put, without rope and without argument. A draft team that does not shy is worth two teams that do, which is why the working appears in building accounts a century before it appears in any bestiary.

rego-animal.name: Drive the Herd
rego-animal.gloss: Move a herd as one thing, over ground no drover would have chosen, without dogs and without losses at the river.

rego-animal.name: The Borrowed Eye
rego-animal.gloss: Send a beast where you would otherwise have to go, and hold it to the errand. A hawk on the ridge is a scout who cannot be bribed, and nobody thinks to look for the scholar who never left her tower.

rego-animal.name: Bring the Pack to Heel
rego-animal.gloss: Call whatever hunts in the country around you and hold it to your order for the length of a fight. Between fights the same binding keeps a university in meat, which is the part the charters actually mention.

rego-aquam.name: Turn the Channel
rego-aquam.gloss: Send water down the ditch you meant it to take, and keep it there through a season. Irrigation is the oldest application and still the one that pays for the rest.

rego-aquam.name: Raise the Weir
rego-aquam.gloss: Hold a river at a height it did not agree to. A weir that need not be built of stone can be put where the mill wants it rather than where the ground allows.

rego-aquam.name: Stand the Water Off
rego-aquam.gloss: Compel water to refuse the shape of a wave, and stand behind it. A wall of held water turns a great deal that a wall of stone does not, and can be dismissed when the siege lifts.

rego-aquam.name: The Held Breath
rego-aquam.gloss: Compel the water already inside a body to stop moving. Nothing is added and nothing is taken away, which is why three universities record the result as a natural death and the fourth has stopped recording it at all.

rego-aquam.name: Shut the Harbour Mouth
rego-aquam.gloss: Bind a stretch of water to hold in both directions at once: nothing crosses it, and nothing thrown across it arrives. Coastal universities keep a warden on the working the way inland ones keep a gatekeeper.

rego-auram.name: Set the Wind
rego-auram.gloss: Put the wind where a sail wants it, for as long as the crossing takes. Timber and stone arrive on the day they were promised, which quietly changes what a university is able to plan.

rego-auram.name: Step on the Air
rego-auram.gloss: Compel a column of air to take a footfall. Not flight: one stride that ends somewhere a stride should not reach, and a long argument afterwards about whether you were ever off the ground.

rego-auram.name: Turn the Storm Aside
rego-auram.gloss: Bind weather to go around a place rather than through it. The neighbours get the weather, and the literature on whether that is actionable is longer than the literature on the working.

rego-auram.name: The Held Gale
rego-auram.gloss: Hold a gale in one place and stand inside it. Everything in reach is being pushed at once, the caster included, which is why the working is never taught apart from the stride that gets her out of it.

rego-corpus.name: Still the Limb
rego-corpus.gloss: Hold a body to its stance, one part at a time — usually your own. Flesh that has been told not to give does not give, and the surgeons found this useful a long time before the duellists did.

rego-corpus.name: The Steady Hand
rego-corpus.gloss: Compel a hand to keep the line true past the hour at which fatigue would have spoiled it. Every accurate diagram in a great library is downstream of somebody holding this working over somebody else's wrist.

rego-corpus.name: Puppet Flesh
rego-corpus.gloss: Move a body that is not moving itself. The working does not distinguish between a corpse and a sleeper; the setting calls it necromancy, and the charters distinguish very carefully indeed.

rego-corpus.name: The Lengthened Term
rego-corpus.gloss: Compel a failing body to keep the arrangement it already has. It adds nothing and heals nothing; it only declines the ending, and the archmages who hold it are careful never to file it beside Puppet Flesh, which is the same insight pointed at a body that has already stopped.

rego-corpus.name: The Unclaimed Body
rego-corpus.gloss: Bind a body whose owner has gone, and set it to work that nobody is now in a position to object to on its behalf. It is the cheapest labour a university can field, and the only kind that has ever closed one.

rego-fatum.name: Hold the Lot
rego-fatum.gloss: Hold a chance to the shape it already had. It cannot make an unlikely thing happen; it can stop a likely one from being spoiled, and across a hundred experiments that is worth a great deal more.

rego-fatum.name: The Kept Oath
rego-fatum.gloss: Bind a promise to its own keeping, so that the breaking of it is the thing that costs. Gods whose worshippers swear on this collect on the oath rather than on the sentiment, and the ledgers show the difference.

rego-fatum.name: Turn the Ill Hour Aside
rego-fatum.gloss: Take a misfortune that was arriving here and hold it somewhere else for a while. It postpones and does not cancel, and the literature is unusually careful about the difference.

rego-fatum.name: The Appointed Hour
rego-fatum.gloss: Fix the hour at which a thing ends, and hold it there. Nothing brings it forward and nothing puts it off, and the scholars who take it rarely say afterwards which of those two halves they wanted.

rego-fatum.name: The Settled Question
rego-fatum.gloss: Bind an outcome and let the world find its own route to it. Every step between here and there still has to be walked; none of them can now go anywhere else, and a god who is owed the ending is owed everything on the way.

rego-herbam.name: Set the Graft
rego-herbam.gloss: Compel a cutting to take, and to take the way the grafter intended rather than the way the tree would have preferred. An orchard planted under it comes into bearing years early.

rego-herbam.name: The Obedient Coppice
rego-herbam.gloss: Hold a wood to the lengths a builder asked for, so that the poles come out of it already straight and already the right size. Carpenters describe the result as timber that has been argued with.

rego-herbam.name: Close the Hedge
rego-herbam.gloss: Bind a hedge to go on closing its own gaps. Nothing that goes through it does so at speed, and nothing that goes through it does so twice.

rego-herbam.name: The Standing Timber
rego-herbam.gloss: Compel green timber to hold the shape of seasoned timber for as long as it is under load. A hall can then be raised in the season the wood was cut, which is the whole of the trick and also the whole of the risk.

rego-ignem.name: Bank the Forge
rego-ignem.gloss: Hold a fire at exactly the heat the work wants, for as long as the work takes. Smelters who have it waste no charge and no charcoal, and can say beforehand what a furnace will yield.

rego-ignem.name: Hold the Fire Off
rego-ignem.gloss: Compel a fire to keep its distance from a named thing. Every library that survives its first arson puts the working on the syllabus permanently, and every library has a first arson.

rego-ignem.name: Drive the Flame
rego-ignem.gloss: Take a fire somebody else lit and tell it where to go. It costs nothing to start, which makes an enemy's own torches the cheapest armament available on the field.

rego-ignem.name: The Walled Fire
rego-ignem.gloss: Bind a fire into a standing ring and stand in the middle of it. The same compulsion that keeps it burning where it was put is what keeps it off the mage who put it there.

rego-imaginem.name: Hold the Likeness
rego-imaginem.gloss: Compel an image to stay exactly as it was set down, so that the tenth copy of a diagram is still the first. Scriptoria that hold it stop losing figures to the slow drift of careful hands.

rego-imaginem.name: The Turned Glance
rego-imaginem.gloss: Compel an eye to travel past you rather than to you. Nothing about you changes; the looking does, and afterwards nobody can say what they were looking at instead.

rego-imaginem.name: Show the Working
rego-imaginem.gloss: Hold the image of a working in the air where a class can walk around it. The difference between describing a proof and standing inside one is most of what a professor is for.

rego-imaginem.name: The Standing Demonstration
rego-imaginem.gloss: Hold one demonstration steady for a whole term, so that the lecture, the argument about the lecture, and the plates for the book are all taken from the same unmoving thing.

rego-limen.name: Hold the Door
rego-limen.gloss: Compel a threshold to keep meaning what it means, against anything arguing otherwise.

rego-limen.name: Step Across
rego-limen.gloss: Treat two thresholds as the same threshold for exactly one stride.

rego-limen.name: Seal the Way
rego-limen.gloss: Bind a threshold shut and make the binding argue back. The defensive half of the same insight that opens portals, which is why forbidding Limen closes both directions at once.

rego-limen.name: Open the Portal
rego-limen.gloss: Hold a threshold open onto a sky that is not yours. Everything the multiverse does to a universe begins here, which is why contracts.md §8 requires this cell in every v1 build.

rego-limen.name: The Standing Gate
rego-limen.gloss: A portal that does not have to be argued into existence each time. Declares no portal-stability effect and never will: the raid's termination guarantee is a proof, not an observation (contracts.md §1.6).

rego-mentem.name: Hold the Attention
rego-mentem.gloss: Keep a mind on the thing in front of it. Unglamorous, and the single largest effect on how fast a university actually teaches.

rego-mentem.name: The Patient Lesson
rego-mentem.gloss: Compel a mind to keep returning to a difficulty instead of routing around it.

rego-mentem.name: Kindle Devotion
rego-mentem.gloss: Bind an ordinary reverence into a durable one. Gods whose scholars know this working are noticeably better funded, and there is a long literature on whether that is cheating.

rego-mentem.name: The Shared Mind
rego-mentem.gloss: Hold teacher and student in one attention, so that the lesson does not have to survive the trip between them.

rego-nomen.name: Call by Name
rego-nomen.gloss: Say a thing's name in the imperative and have it arrive. The oldest complaint in the literature is that it does not specify in what condition.

rego-nomen.name: Write the Name Down
rego-nomen.gloss: Bind a name to a page so firmly that a scribe who cannot pronounce it can still copy it correctly.

rego-nomen.name: Keep the Name Close
rego-nomen.gloss: Hold your own name in your own keeping, so that it does not answer when someone else uses it. Taught in the same term as Compel by Name, by professors who consider that an ethics curriculum.

rego-nomen.name: Compel by Name
rego-nomen.gloss: Hold a mage by her name and take what she knows out through it. The second theft vector, and the one that leaves a mark — which is why a universe may want to close exactly one of the two.

rego-nomen.name: The Bound Servant
rego-nomen.gloss: Call a thing by a name it cannot refuse and keep it. In a True Naming universe this is either the strongest working in the subset or the reason your archmage now belongs to someone else.

rego-terram.name: Set the Stone
rego-terram.gloss: Put a block exactly where it belongs, on the first attempt, without a crane.

rego-terram.name: Raise the Course
rego-terram.gloss: Lay a whole course of a wall as one working. This is vision §4's worked example: earth magic building universities faster is a number here, not a special case in code.

rego-terram.name: Quarry Without Hands
rego-terram.gloss: Compel stone out of a seam that no crew could reach and down to where it is wanted.

rego-terram.name: The Vaulted Hall
rego-terram.gloss: Hold a span up while it is built, so that it can be built at a size that could not have stood while unfinished. Every great library in the subset is one of these.

rego-umbra.name: Hold the Shadow Still
rego-umbra.gloss: Compel a shadow to stay where it was cast while the thing that cast it moves. Nobody watches a shadow; they watch what it says is standing there.

rego-umbra.name: The Lent Shadow
rego-umbra.gloss: Put your shadow somewhere you are not and leave it there working. It is a poor likeness and an excellent alibi, and it holds for exactly as long as nobody speaks to it.

rego-umbra.name: Step by Shadow
rego-umbra.gloss: Enter one darkness and leave another in a single stride. It wants a shadow at both ends, which is why the wardens of careful universities keep the courtyards lit all night.

rego-umbra.name: The Held Dark
rego-umbra.gloss: Hold the dark of a place still and full until it stops being an absence and starts being something standing in the room. Everyone inside is hidden from everyone else, which favours whoever knew that going in.

rego-vim.name: Steady the Working
rego-vim.gloss: Hold a half-formed working still while you finish it. Most failed research is not wrong, merely interrupted, and this is the working that stops the interruption from counting.

rego-vim.name: Turn the Casting
rego-vim.gloss: Put your will between a working and the thing it was aimed at. The oldest defensive result in the literature, and still the one that decides duels between people who both have it.

rego-vim.name: The Working Kept in Iron
rego-vim.gloss: Bind a working into a thing, so that it goes on being cast without being cast again. Every well-appointed laboratory in the subset is a shelf of these, and every one of them was somebody's thesis.

rego-vim.name: Forbid the Casting
rego-vim.gloss: Bind the air of a place against workings that are not yours. Argument continues inside it; magic does not, and the distinction is enforced by the room rather than by anybody standing in it.

rego-vim.name: The Standing Prohibition
rego-vim.gloss: Hold a place against a whole body of magic indefinitely, without a god's edict and without a god's leave. A scholar who has one has written a ruling nobody signed; universities that keep one do not advertise it, and universities that have lost one write about very little else.
